subject: general
question: Doubly-charged helium ions are also known as which of the following?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Alpha particles**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__ **

__
 
• **Alpha particles:**
 
• Alpha particles are composed of two protons and two neutrons, making them identical to the nucleus of a helium atom.
 
• This composition results in a double positive charge (He²⁺).
 
• They are emitted during the radioactive decay of some heavy atomic nuclei.
 
• Alpha particles have relatively low penetration power and can be stopped by a sheet of paper.
 
• They have a relatively high ionizing power, meaning they can easily knock electrons out of atoms.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gamma particles:**
 
• Gamma rays are high-energy electromagnetic radiation.
 
• They have no mass or charge.
 
• Gamma rays are emitted from atomic nuclei during radioactive decay.
 
• They have high penetration power and can pass through thick materials.
 
• Gamma rays are highly ionizing.
 
• **X-rays:**
 
• X-rays are also electromagnetic radiation, but they have lower energy than gamma rays.
 
• They are produced when electrons are decelerated or when inner-shell electrons transition to lower energy levels.
 
• X-rays have varying penetration power depending on their energy.
 
• They are used in medical imaging and industrial applications.
 
• X-rays are ionizing radiation.
 
• **Beta particles:**
 
• Beta particles are high-speed electrons or positrons emitted during radioactive decay.
 
• They have a single negative or positive charge.
 
• Beta particles have greater penetration power than alpha particles but less than gamma rays.
 
• They are involved in beta decay, a type of radioactive transformation.
 
• Beta particles are ionizing radiation.
